summary: Targeted re-check (not a full re-review) of the one security-sensitive item in fix commit 50e04c0: the extraction of the user-search exact-match gate from app/app/api/users/search/route.ts into the new shared module app/src/lib/userSearchQuery.ts, now also imported client-side by both search UIs. All four requested properties confirmed intact, no regression, no new findings. (1) Pure relocation: `git diff HEAD~1 -- app/app/api/users/search/route.ts` shows the removed inline block and the new module body are identical apart from the inline return type being named `UserSearchFilter` and comments added — EMAIL_SHAPE is byte-identical (/^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/), the email branch is still `equals` + mode insensitive, the username branch still goes through normalizeUsername and still requires norm.valid && norm.username, and null is still returned for everything else. No contains/startsWith/endsWith/search operator anywhere in the module, the route, or either UI (the only `contains` hit in the diff is DOM Node.contains for click-outside at UserSearch.tsx:111). (2) Route order unchanged and still correct: requireAuth (401 on AuthError) -> checkRateLimit(namespace users:search, 60/3600, failMode closed, keyed on uid) -> 429 -> only then `exactMatchFilter(q)`; the filter builder is a pure function with no I/O, so moving it out of the file cannot create a pre-guard path. Self-exclusion intact at route.ts:52-55 as `where: { ...filter, id: { not: uid } }` — `id` is written after the spread and exactMatchFilter's two literal shapes contain no `id` key, so no query value can override it. (3) Client-bundle safe: transitive import closure of userSearchQuery is exactly userSearchQuery -> src/lib/username -> src/lib/nameModeration, which has zero imports. No Prisma/@prisma, no src/db/client, no firebase-admin, no process.env, no require() anywhere in that closure — the implementer's 'structural typing, no Prisma import' claim verified against the actual file, not the summary. UserSearchFilter is a hand-written union, not Prisma.UserWhereInput. No new client exposure either: src/lib/username + nameModeration were already reachable from the mobile bundle via mobile/src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx. The client-side gate being readable/bypassable in the bundle is irrelevant because the server re-runs the same function after auth+rate-limit, and the gate encodes no secret (the username rules and reserved list already shipped to both bundles). (4) searchFailureMessage(status) returns one of three hardcoded literals and takes only a number|null; res.json() is called ONLY inside the res.ok branch in both UIs, so no error body, code, stack or internal detail is ever read on the failure path, let alone rendered. 429 gets distinct copy without echoing the numeric status. Verified by invocation, not by grep: ran a 6-case adversarial fixture suite (28 malformed/partial/injection inputs incl. 'bob%', '%', "'; DROP TABLE users;--", '{"$ne":null}', 'bob@example', '../../etc/passwd', reserved names, 31 chars) asserting every one returns null from both exactMatchFilter and isSearchableQuery, that emitted filters contain no partial-match operator and no id key, that the username path is normalised to [a-z0-9-], that id:{not:uid} survives the spread, and that no failure message matches /\d{3}|Error:|prisma|stack|INTERNAL|UNAUTHORIZED|RATE_LIMITED/ — 6/6 pass against the real module alongside the 7 existing tests/api/usersSearch.route.test.ts cases (13/13). Then proved the suite is load-bearing per the repo's prove-fail rule: a scratchpad copy of the module with contains/startsWith swapped in turns 3 of the 6 red ('expected {"email":{"contains":"bob@example.com"...} not to match /contains|startsWith|.../'). Both probes were created and deleted outside the tracked tree; `git status --porcelain` is empty, read-only respected. Secret scan of the whole fix diff (api[_-]?key|secret|token=|password|PRIVATE KEY|sk_live|sk_test|Bearer|process.env): zero hits. Dependency audit intentionally not re-run — the commit touches no package.json and no lockfile, so the audit result is unchanged from security-reviewer-2026-09-20T015500Z.
goal: Narrow re-verification that the search-gate extraction in 50e04c0 preserved exact-match-only matching, kept requireAuth/checkRateLimit/self-exclusion wrapping every call, is safe to bundle client-side, and that searchFailureMessage leaks nothing.

findings.issue: PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS COMMIT (alias landed in 36da05a, PR #120) and NOT a vulnerability today — recorded only so it is on the record. `@app` maps to the whole of app/src for the mobile bundle, and app/src also holds server-only, secret-bearing modules: db/client.ts (PrismaClient), lib/firebaseAdmin.ts, lib/requireAuth.ts, lib/redis.ts, api/stripe.ts, social/crypto/tokenEncryption.ts. Nothing in this diff imports any of them (verified: userSearchQuery's transitive closure is username -> nameModeration, both dependency-free), and this commit's addition of the same-shaped "@app/*": ["./src/*"] to app/tsconfig.json only affects the Node-side typecheck program, not a client bundle. But the alias grants mobile client code a spelled-out path to server modules, so a future careless `@app/db/...` or `@app/lib/requireAuth` import would be a resolvable path rather than a build error.
findings.reproduction: No attack path in the current tree — there is no such import to exploit, so per adversarial self-verification this is info, not high. Latent form: add `import { prisma } from "@app/db/client"` to any mobile/src file and vite resolves it into the WebView bundle.
findings.fix: Out of scope for this fix commit; do not touch it here. Optional follow-up ticket: narrow the mobile alias to the directories the SPA actually shares (e.g. @app/lib, @app/game, @app/components, @app/design) instead of all of src, or add a hygiene/lint check that fails when mobile/src imports @app/db, @app/api or a known server-only lib.

learnings.insight: Extracting a security gate into a shared module that is ALSO client-bundled makes the module's transitive import closure part of the security review, not just its body. The body here was clean, but the real question was what `import { normalizeUsername } from "./username"` drags along — one hop further, nameModeration, has zero imports, which is the only reason the extraction is bundle-safe. Had username.ts imported anything from src/db or src/lib/redis, a pure-looking three-line function would have pulled Prisma or a Redis client into a Capacitor WebView bundle. The implementer's 'no Prisma import' claim was true of the file but says nothing about hop 2.
learnings.action: When reviewing a lib that crosses the server/client boundary, walk the full import closure (rg imports in the file, then in each import, until it bottoms out) and assert the closure contains no process.env, PrismaClient, firebase-admin, redis or crypto-secret module. Do not stop at the direct imports of the changed file, and do not accept the implementer's summary as the evidence.

learnings.insight: `where: { ...exactMatchFilter(q), id: { not: uid } }` is safe here for two independent reasons and it is worth knowing which: the spread source is a closed union of two object literals with no `id` key, AND `id` is written after the spread so it wins on any collision. The ordering is what makes it robust to a future edit that widens the filter shape. If someone ever reorders to `{ id: {not: uid}, ...filter }`, a filter that gains an `id` key silently deletes self-exclusion and the route starts returning the caller to themselves (and, worse, any row the filter names).
learnings.action: Keep server-derived constraints (id/self-exclusion, tenant/owner scoping, soft-delete filters) AFTER any spread of a request-derived fragment in a Prisma `where`. Flag the reverse order in review even when the current filter shape makes it harmless.

learnings.insight: userSearchQuery.ts now has three production callers and still no direct unit test — the existing tests/api/usersSearch.route.test.ts covers it only transitively through the route, so a client-only weakening (e.g. someone loosens isSearchableQuery to let 2-char prefixes through to save a keystroke) would not turn anything red. I proved a fixture suite over exactMatchFilter/isSearchableQuery/searchFailureMessage is cheap (6 cases, ~380ms including the route tests) and that it goes red 3/6 when contains/startsWith is substituted, so this gap is closeable in one small file. The verifier's own prior ping about searchFailureMessage having zero tests still stands and is the same file.
learnings.action: Add app/tests/lib/userSearchQuery.test.ts asserting: a malformed/partial/injection fixture array all returns null from BOTH exactMatchFilter and isSearchableQuery (the negative guard against real positive fixtures), that emitted filters never JSON-stringify to contain contains|startsWith|endsWith|search, that '@BobSmith' -> { username: 'bobsmith' }, and searchFailureMessage(429)/(500)/(null) are three distinct static strings matching no /\d{3}|Error:|stack/. Import the real module — do not re-implement the regex in the test.

learnings.insight: Narrow re-check scope: 2 files re-audited in depth (userSearchQuery.ts 78 lines new, users/search/route.ts diff -27/+1), 1 info finding (pre-existing, not introduced), 0 warnings, 0 critical/high. 13 tests run green (6 ad-hoc adversarial + 7 existing route), 1 prove-fail probe executed and reverted, repo tree left clean. pnpm audit deliberately skipped: no package.json or lockfile change in 50e04c0, so the prior audit result from security-reviewer-2026-09-20T015500Z still holds.
learnings.action: A post-loop-back security re-check scoped to 'did this property survive the refactor' is ~1/5 the cost of a re-review and is the right shape when the diff's security surface is one extracted pure function. Keep scoping re-checks this way rather than re-running the full pass; but require the re-check to invoke the extracted unit, since the whole risk of an extraction is silent behaviour drift that a diff read can miss.
